title: Implement trusted V21 Open Library qualification command
goal: Add the smallest trusted TIA Portal V21 Openness command that converts an operator-supplied Siemens Open Library V19 .zal19 archive into a deterministic native V21 qualified-library archive plus machine-readable qualification evidence. Migration is a one-time qualification operation, never part of normal project generation.
scope: Modify only the trusted src/TiaV21Worker boundary unless a tiny adjacent non-Siemens test/helper change is strictly required. Do not modify Domain, PlcCompiler, SiemensBackend semantics, GeneratorCli, workflows, task files, prompts, or IndustrialMDE.
Preserve the existing TiaV21Worker smoke-test CLI behavior. Add an explicit qualify-library command/path rather than overloading normal SCL acceptance semantics.

The qualification command receives an absolute operator-controlled source .zal19 path, an absolute qualification output root, an absolute manifest/diagnostics JSON path, and optionally an absolute work root. The vendor archive itself must never be copied into Git output or committed.
Before opening TIA Portal, compute and record the exact SHA256 of the source .zal19 archive.

Use TIA Portal V21 Openness previous-version archive retrieval via GlobalLibraries.RetrieveWithUpgrade(sourceArchive, targetDirectory, OpenMode.ReadWrite). Do not use OpenWithUpgrade as a substitute for the archived .zal19 qualification path and do not add migration to any normal generator/project-assembly path.

After retrieval/upgrade, save the user global library before archiving it. Create a compressed native V21 archive with an explicit .zal21 file name using the V21 UserGlobalLibrary.Archive API and LibraryArchivationMode.Compressed.

Derive a stable qualification identity from source archive SHA256 plus the exact TIA/Openness build identity. Do not silently overwrite an existing qualification identity whose manifest/hash does not match the current source/build; fail deterministically instead.

Reopen/retrieve the produced native .zal21 archive with the current-version Retrieve API, not RetrieveWithUpgrade, as the bounded OLQ-001 proof that the resulting archive is native V21 and usable by V21 Openness. Close/dispose opened libraries cleanly.

Record machine-readable evidence including success/failure, source path basename only (not required to expose operator directories), source SHA256, TIA Portal/Openness V21 assembly/build identity, qualification identity, qualified archive file name, qualified archive SHA256, native-reopen result, and failure diagnostics when applicable.

Keep detailed fbValve_Solenoid contract discovery and master-copy/project materialization out of this task; those belong to OL-001/OL-002. If the real V19 archive cannot be upgraded/retrieved/reopened as native V21, report explicit BLOCKED/failure evidence rather than claiming qualification success.

requirements: Existing TiaV21Worker SCL smoke-test invocation remains backward compatible and its behavior is not weakened.
A distinct qualify-library command/path exists and validates absolute input/output paths plus the expected .zal19 source extension before TIA processing.
Source archive SHA256 is computed before TIA Portal processes the library.

The implementation uses TIA Portal V21 GlobalLibraries.RetrieveWithUpgrade for the previous-version compressed archive, saves the retrieved UserGlobalLibrary, then creates a compressed archive with an explicit .zal21 name.
The produced native archive is verified through current-version GlobalLibraries.Retrieve rather than another upgrade call.

Qualification identity is deterministic from source SHA256 plus TIA/Openness build identity, and an existing mismatched identity/archive/manifest causes deterministic failure rather than silent overwrite.

A machine-readable manifest/diagnostics JSON records source SHA256, exact V21 build identity, qualification identity, output archive name/hash, native reopen status, and actionable failure information without committing or embedding the vendor library payload.
No Siemens.Engineering dependency is introduced outside src/TiaV21Worker and no normal generator path performs V19-to-V21 migration.

Existing Linux SiemensBackend tests and Motor/ValveConfig generator regressions remain green; candidate code is reviewed from source/diff evidence and is not executed on the Windows/TIA runner before trusted merge.
tia: After independent review and trusted merge, TiaV21Worker builds on the TIA V21 Windows runner against the installed V21 net48 Openness assemblies.
Using the real operator-controlled Siemens Open Library V19 .zal19 archive, the trusted qualify-library command records its source SHA256 and exact TIA/Openness V21 build identity.

The trusted run successfully retrieves/upgrades the V19 archive, saves it, emits a compressed native .zal21 qualified archive, computes the output SHA256, and records the deterministic qualification identity.
The produced .zal21 can be retrieved/opened through the current-version Retrieve API without another upgrade step; otherwise the qualification result is failure/BLOCKED evidence.
A second run for the same source SHA256 and TIA build is deterministic and does not silently replace a different qualification result.
Durable GitHub evidence contains manifest/diagnostics and hashes only; the vendor .zal19/.zal21 payload remains outside the public repository.
